newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - WALL STREET JOURNAL - AUG 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - WALL STREET JOURNAL - AUG 12.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Tuesday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal.
* United Parcel Service and Teamsters union representatives met with Labor Secretary Alexis Herman to jump-start their stalled contract negotiations.
* Credit Suisse Group agreed to buy Winterthur Group and said they would merge.
* The FASB rejected Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan's request to soften a plan that requires firms to adjust earnings to reflect changes in the value of derivatives.
* Thailand's neighbors contributed more than expected towards the country's currency-crisis rescue package.
* Norfolk Southern and CSX offered to buy Delaware Otsego for $19 a share.
* Stocks recouped some of last Friday's losses, as the Dow Industrials rose 30.89 to 8062.11
* Hedge funds are seeing more money pour into them for the first time in four years.
* Reader's Digest replaced its CEO James Schadt with former CEO George Grune.
* Quick & Reilly hired investment bankers to solicit the company.
* Nordstrom posted a 31.0 percent increase in second-quarter income.
* Shoney's reached an agreement with dissident shareholders to add some of them to its board.
* PolyGram said Andre Harrell quit as president and chief executive of Motown Records. (--New York newsdesk 212-859-1610)
